entities.summary:
Titus Geganius Macerinus (titus-geganius-macerinus) was a Roman politician and consul in 492 BC, instrumental in passing laws aimed at reducing debt and promoting economic growth in Rome.

Macerinus was born into a prominent patrician family in Rome and received a traditional education in Greek and Roman literature, law, and politics.

As consul, Macerinus worked closely with his co-consul, Publius Minucius Augurinus, to pass laws that aimed to reduce debt and promote economic growth in Rome.

Macerinus's legacy is complex and multifaceted, reflecting both the success and the challenges faced by the Roman Republic in its early years.

In the annals of Roman history, Macerinus stands as a testament to the power of politics and the importance of economic stability in shaping the fate of nations.
